newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Intra-ASEAN trade jumps 17 percent in 1994-95.
newsitem.headline: Intra-ASEAN trade jumps 17 percent in 1994-95.

text.p: Trade among the seven members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations jumped about 17 percent in 1995 over 1994, ASEAN said on Monday.

Intra-ASEAN trade in both goods within and outside the Common Effective Preferrential Tariff (CEPT) rose to $66.5 billion in 1995 from $56.6 billion in 1994, ASEAN Secretary-General Ajit Singh told a news conference.
"The countries experiencing the highest percentage growth of intra-ASEAN trade are the Philippines, 64 percent, and Malaysia, 20 percent.
"In absolute terms, the member countries which experienced the highest growth in intra-ASEAN exports are Singapore, $3.6 billion, and Malaysia, $3.0 billion," Singh said.
He gave details of an ASEAN secretariat trade analysis ahead of meetings of the council of the ASEAN Free Trade Area (AFTA) and ASEAN economic ministers in Jakarta this week.
ASEAN groups Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei, the Philippines and Vietnam.
Singh said four major sectors accounted for about 80 percent of intra-ASEAN trade in 1994-95.

These were mechanical and electrical appliances, which rose $5.6 billion and accounted for 55.7 percent of the trade increase, plastics and "articles" around $1.2 billion or 11.23 percent, chemical industry products $730 million or 6.8 percent, and base metals and "articles" $680 million or 6.35 percent.
